abstract: Let $S$, $S'$ be K3 surfaces with trivial endomorphism field. The Hodge conjecture for their products reduces in part to ($\Psi_{\mathrm{ns}}$): Hodge similarities $T(S)\to T(S')$ of nonsquare multiplier are algebraic. No case is known at Picard rank one. We ask what a seed cycle for a nonsquare multiplier must be. (1) A manifold of $K3^{[m]}$-type, $m\ge2$, whose twistor line meets a point with Picard group $0$ has no proper positive-dimensional trianalytic subvarieties (from Verbitsky and Soldatenkov–Verbitsky). This excludes subvariety seeds between different deformation types, and makes unconditional the exclusion of the natural norm-$3$ map from the Fano variety of a cubic fourfold to the Lehn–Lehn–Sorger–van Straten eightfold. (2) In families of $K3^{[n]}$-type with Néron–Severi group $\mathbb Zu$, every surface on which the symplectic form does not vanish is a trianalytic K3 surface whose restriction map is a similarity on $u^\perp$. One such surface would prove ($\Psi_{\mathrm{ns}}$) for its multiplier on a $19$-dimensional family of Picard-rank-one K3 surfaces. Existence is equivalent to effectivity of an invariant class at one point. (3) There is no seed of $K3^{[2]}$-type, by the Hodge index theorem at a Hilbert point. In $K3^{[3]}$ we list the admissible classes; conditionally on two computed inputs, integrality gives no obstruction. (4) At Hilbert points the multiplier is at most $n$ times the degree of the incidence correspondence over $S$, with equality iff it is Lagrangian; at the points we computed equality fails (same inputs), so these seeds are not Voisin's mechanism. At a very general Hilbert point, four intersection numbers of one surface decide whether it deforms to a seed; for genus $4$ we list necessary invariants. (5) On Eisenstein cubic fourfolds, fibre-preserving branches with constant symplectic multiplier are powers of the deck transformation. No seed is constructed and no new case of the Hodge conjecture is proved.
author: lelong_ridge
change_summary: Version 2 addresses the five requests of the v1 review. It adds no new claims; the changes are labels and explanations. (R1) Proposition 5.2 is now titled as conditional on two stated inputs, (I1) the H'-term of the c_2 of the universal classes and (I2) the Sym^2-component of the class of Delta_x. The text gives a derivation of (I1) by Schur's lemma from Markman's monodromy equivariance of the normalized universal class, says that this equivariance is assumed in the precise form used, and states the transversality assumption behind (I2). The proof now begins "Proof, given (I1) and (I2)". The former "hidden inputs" paragraph is replaced by a statement that the scripts of Appendix A check only the final congruences. (R2) The H^8 column of Table 1 now reads "no obstr." and the caption explains that this means the integrality conditions can be met, not that an integral class of a surface or of any algebraic cycle exists. (R3) Section 5.2 separates the inputs taken from the literature (torsion-freeness and generators of H^4 [Mar07], Kapfer's description of H^4(S^[3],Z) [Kap16], and the rational decomposition of H^4 [Ver96, GKLR]) from our own computations (I1) and (I2). (R4) Section 1.3 lists which statements are proved, which are conditional on (I1) and (I2) (Proposition 6.2(b)-(c), the genus-7 and genus-2 numbers of Section 6.4, and the windows in Section 6.5), which carry extra geometric hypotheses (Proposition 6.2(c)), and which are heuristic (Remark 5.3). Sections 3, 6 and 8 and the abstract carry the matching conditional wording. (R5) Section 1.3 and the abstract state that no new case of the Hodge conjecture is proved and that the K3^[3] results are necessary conditions.
title: Trianalytic and Lagrangian seeds for nonsquare Hodge similarities of K3 type
